title: What can you do if you forget a photo vault password?
description: Forgot your photo vault password? Check for a recovery key, an active unlock method and a backup before you do anything that erases the vault.

sections.h: Start by leaving the vault alone
p: If you forget your photo vault password, first leave the vault and the app exactly as they are. Do not clear app storage and do not uninstall. Whether you can get back in depends on what you still hold: a recovery key, an unlock method that is still active on the phone, or a backup together with the secret that belongs to it.

Some photo vault apps offer no recovery path at all, because the secret never leaves the phone. Encrypted storage works on the same principle, so the useful question is not how to reset a password but which copy of the key you still have.
Go through these checks before you try the unlock screen again and again. Each one is quick, and none of them changes the vault.
list: Find the recovery key you saved when you created the vault, and check that it is the copy you kept away from the phone.
Check whether biometric, phone screen-lock or in-app pattern unlock was switched on, and whether it still opens the vault.
Find the newest encrypted backup file, and note which passphrase or recovery key was active when you made it.
Write down when you last changed the passphrase, because older backups keep the secret they were made with.
Try each secret you hold once, checking caps lock and spelling, rather than guessing variations.

p: NullKey has no account reset, and Alvento holds no copy of your vault, so Alvento cannot recover a forgotten passphrase or missing files. A saved recovery key can open an existing vault. Biometric unlock can open the vault without the passphrase while it stays enabled. Screen-lock and pattern unlock pause after an app update or seven days without typing the passphrase, so they may not help after a long gap. A restore needs an empty vault on that phone and the secret that belongs to that backup.
The honest limit: if you have lost both the passphrase and the recovery key, Alvento cannot reset access, and the encrypted data stays inaccessible.

Encryption is designed so that stored files cannot be read without the right key. That protects them from someone who copies the files, but it also means the company that made the app often cannot open them either, because it never held the key. A reset link or a support ticket cannot rebuild a key that exists only in your hands.

Clearing app data or uninstalling can remove the local vault on many phones, and that copy may be the only one you have. A factory reset can work the same way. Treat those steps as a last resort, and only after you have checked whether a backup exists somewhere else.

sections.h: Set up a way back before you need it
p: The best time to prepare for a forgotten password is while you still remember it. Save the recovery key somewhere separate from the phone, make an encrypted backup, and keep the secret for that backup with it rather than in the same folder as the file. Then run a test restore with a few sample photos into an empty test vault, so you know the process works.
Repeat the backup after important changes, and label each older backup with the secret it needs.

faq.q: Can the app maker reset my photo vault password?
faq.a: It depends on the app. Some makers can reset access through an account, while others hold no copy of your key and cannot help at all. NullKey has no account reset, so a saved recovery key, or a backup together with its secret, is the main route back in.

faq.q: Will reinstalling the app bring my vault back?
faq.a: Usually not, and it can remove what you still have. On many phones, uninstalling or clearing app storage deletes the local vault, and a fresh install starts with nothing in it. Keep the app and its data in place while you check your recovery options.

faq.q: What if I changed my passphrase after making a backup?
faq.a: The old backup keeps the secret it was made with, because changing the passphrase does not rewrite earlier backup files. Use the passphrase or recovery key that belongs to that specific backup. If you cannot find it, that backup may not open, so check your older secrets first.
